parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish جوز (cevz), from Arabic جَوْز (jawz), from Middle Persian 𐭢𐭥𐭦 (gʿz /⁠gōz⁠/); see Old Armenian ընկոյզ (ənkoyz) for more.

parole.significato: System of beliefs dealing with soul, deity or life after death.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish دین, from Arabic دِين (dīn) with some influence from Middle Persian (see the Arabic term for details).
From Ottoman Turkish درهم (dirhem), from Arabic دِرْهَم (dirham), from Middle Persian 𐭦𐭥𐭦𐭭 (zʿzn), from Ancient Greek δραχμή (drakhmḗ). Doublet of drahma and drahoma.

parole.significato: elephant, a mammal of the order Proboscidea, having a large trunk
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فیل (fil, “elephant”), from Arabic فِيل (fīl), from Middle Persian pyl (/⁠pīl⁠/), ultimately from Akkadian 𒄠𒋛 (/⁠pīru⁠/).

parole.significato: pistachio, the nutlike fruit produced by any tree in the species Pistacia vera
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فستق (fıstık), from Arabic فُسْتُق (fustuq), from Middle Persian pstk' (pistag).
From Ottoman Turkish هندسه (hendese), from Arabic هَنْدَسَة (handasa), from Middle Persian.

parole.significato: camphor, a waxy, colorless solid with a strong aroma extracted from the wood of the camphor tree
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كافور (kâfur, “camphor”), borrowed from Arabic كَافُور (kāfūr, “camphor”), possibly borrowed from Middle Persian 𐭪𐭠𐭯𐭥𐭫 (kʾpʿl /⁠kāpūr⁠/), borrowed from an Austronesian language, from Proto-Austronesian *qapuʀ.

parole.significato: good (commonly used when referring to the smell of something)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مسك, from Arabic مِسْك (misk), from Middle Persian [script needed] (mwšk' /⁠mušk⁠/), from Sanskrit मुष्क (muṣka, “testicle”). Doublet of misk.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مسك (misk), from Arabic مِسْك (misk), from Middle Persian [script needed] (mwšk' /⁠mušk⁠/), from Sanskrit मुष्क (muṣka). Doublet of mis.
From Ottoman Turkish مهندس (mühendis), from Arabic مُهَنْدِس (muhandis), from Middle Persian اندازه (andāza).

parole.significato: Turco-Greek, of or related to the Rumlar, ethnic Greeks living in Turkey and Cyprus

From Ottoman Turkish طاق (tak), from Arabic طَاق (ṭāq), possibly from Middle Persian *tāk, a variant of tʾg (/⁠tāg⁠/, “arch”) (compare modern Persian طاق (tâq, “arch”)). Doublet of taç (“crown; belt”).

parole.significato: a bowl, typically made of metal.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish طاس (tas), which borrowed this from Arabic طَاس (ṭās, “bowl”) (a shortening of طَسْت (ṭast)), from Middle Persian tšt' (tašt), ultimately from the past participle of Proto-Iranian *taš- (“to make, construct; to cut”), from Proto-Indo-European *tetḱ-. Cognate with French tasse.
From Ottoman Turkish یاقوت (yakut), from Arabic يَاقُوت (yāqūt), from Middle Persian y'knd (yâkand, “ruby”). Ultimately from Ancient Greek ὑάκινθος (huákinthos). Unrelated to Yakut.
